study_families.study_label: Study 1: 2017 Snowdonia Marathon field cohort (RTI + psychological factors + saliva sIgA)
study_families.design: Prospective field observational cohort; single-group pre-post marathon design with no non-exercise comparator arm; psychological factors measured prospectively before the race, RTI monitored for 2 weeks before and after.
study_families.training_load: NR beyond habitual-training description at recruitment (not itemised in Methods).
study_families.study_notes: Not pre-registered: 'Both studies received local university ethics committee approval and were conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki (2013) principles without pre-registration' (p.2).

study_families.study_label: Study 2: laboratory crossover (exercise vs seated-rest control)
study_families.design: Randomised, repeated-measures crossover laboratory trial; each participant completed both an exercise (EX: 60 min treadmill running at 65% VO2peak) and a seated-rest control (CON) trial in randomised order, trials separated by >=48 h.
study_families.training_load: Participants recreationally active, 3-9 h/week aerobic exercise (p.3); refrained from alcohol, caffeine, OTC medication and heavy exercise for 24 h before each trial.
study_families.cointerventions: Standardised pre-trial meal (2.2 MJ) and 5 ml/kg water provided before each trial; fluid replaced during trials (3 ml/kg/h water in EX; equivalent 35 ml/kg/d in CON) to offset sweat losses (p.4).
study_families.study_notes: Not pre-registered (see Study 1 note, p.2, applies to both studies).

reports.title: Anxiety and Mood Disturbance Are Prospectively Associated With Respiratory Infection Risk and the Mucosal Immune Response to Exercise
reports.authors: Harrison SE; Edwards JP; Roberts R; Walsh NP
reports.version_date: UNCLEAR - Received 2024-11-15, Revised 2025-09-05, Accepted 2025-09-15 (p.1); specific online-publication date not stated on the pages read.
reports.version_label: Version of record, European Journal of Sport Science 2025;25:e70058 (Original Paper, open access)
reports.inclusion_reason: Two sub-studies each built around an identifiable single bout with pre-bout baseline and post-cessation sampling in adults: Study 1 = 2017 Snowdonia Marathon (saliva pre- and immediately post-race, p.2); Study 2 = 60-min treadmill run at 65% VO2peak vs seated-rest control, saliva pre/immediate-post/+30min (p.4). Direct immune-linked measurement (salivary sIgA, a recognized immune mediator) satisfies immune_link; Study 1 additionally tracks a self-reported clinical outcome (RTI) for 2 weeks post-race.
reports.reviewer_notes: Provisional INCLUDE_A for both sub-studies (no repeated identified exercise bouts in the same people across >=2 events, so Support B does not apply; Study 2's EX-vs-CON crossover is a single exercise bout plus a non-exercise comparator, not a second bout). See unresolved_questions on whether Study 1 and Study 2 should be two cohorts under one study_id or two separate study_families as modelled here.
reports.author_stated_use: NR (no explicit named application such as recovery/return-to-training stated; the paper's framing is mechanistic/monitoring research into psychological-immune links, p.1-2).
author_window_interpretation_locator: p.2 Introduction: 'with lower sIgA levels in saliva ... relating to increased RTI risk'; p.9 Discussion references reduced sIgA as a candidate mechanism for RTI risk. The phrase 'open window' does not appear in the text; the paper's own finding in Study 1 was explicitly NO association between the sIgA change and RTI risk (p.6).

cohorts.baseline_health: RTI-analysis sample excluded n=11 'not healthy on marathon day' (Figure 1); otherwise general marathon-entrant population, no further explicit health-screening criteria reported.
cohorts.age_sex: Recruited/consented n=406 (men n=271, age 46+-9 y, height 177+-12 cm, mass 78+-10 kg, BMI 24+-3; women n=135, age 43+-8 y, height 166+-6 cm, mass 62+-8 kg, BMI 23+-3) (p.2).
cohorts.training_status: Marathon entrants; Discussion notes 'participants in this study were not elite athletes' and that the average age was 'relatively high' (p.9) - i.e. recreational/non-elite.
cohorts.sport: Marathon running (Snowdonia Marathon: mountain/trail terrain, total ascent 939 m, p.2).
cohorts.cohort_notes: Final analysis samples are subsets of the 406 consented: RTI data n=336 (70 excluded: 59 insufficient dataset, 11 not healthy on marathon day); SIgA data n=210 (196 excluded: 101 no saliva sample, 84 incomplete dataset, 6 CV>15%, 5 statistical outlier); combined RTI+SIgA sample n=199 (Figure 1 flow chart, p.3).
cohorts.age_range: NR as an explicit range; mean+-SD by sex given (men 46+-9 y; women 43+-8 y, p.2); authors note the average age was 'relatively high in Study 1' compared with Study 2 and raise possible peri/post-menopausal status in women as a discussion point (p.8), but do not define an older-adult cut-off themselves.

cohorts.baseline_health: Healthy in the 7 days preceding each trial (no respiratory illness symptoms); nonsmokers; no prescription medication during the study or preceding month (p.3).
cohorts.age_sex: n=45 (men n=26, women n=19); All age 22+-3 y, men 21+-2 y, women 23+-4 y (Table 1, p.4); height 174+-9 cm, body mass 72+-10 kg, BMI 24+-3 (All).
cohorts.sport: General aerobic exercise (treadmill running test protocol); not a named competitive sport.
cohorts.cohort_notes: Females naturally menstruating (n=10) or using oral contraceptives (n=4) or a contraceptive implant (n=5); cycle phase matched across EX/CON by testing on the same day of two separate cycles for naturally menstruating women (p.3).
cohorts.age_range: NR as an explicit range; mean+-SD only (Table 1).

report_cohort_links.n_analyzed: 336 (RTI analysis, Table 2); 210 (SIgA/mucosal-immunity analysis); 199 (combined RTI+SIgA regression models, Table 3) - three different denominators for three different analyses within the same cohort (Figure 1 flow chart, p.3).
report_cohort_links.report_specific_population: Subset of the 406 consented runners with sufficient RTI symptom-diary data and/or usable saliva samples per Figure 1 exclusion criteria.
report_cohort_links.link_notes: Single field cohort; denominators differ by outcome measured (RTI-only, SIgA-only, or both) - see Figure 1.

report_cohort_links.n_analyzed: 45 (all participants provided data for both EX and CON trials; no attrition/exclusion reported for Study 2 in the text read).
report_cohort_links.report_specific_population: All 45 consented participants, analysed combined and separately by sex (Table 1; Figure 3 men-only subgroup, n~26).
report_cohort_links.link_notes: Laboratory crossover cohort, independent of Study 1 (different participants, different setting).

sample_sets.group_condition: All runners with usable saliva data (final SIgA sample, n=210)
sample_sets.dose: Snowdonia Marathon (mixed road/trail terrain, total ascent 939 m); men avg completion 4 h 26 min+-46 min, women 4 h 55 min+-49 min
sample_sets.control: No non-exercise control group in Study 1; within-person pre/post comparison only
sample_sets.exercise_end_definition: UNCLEAR - clock-time based sample collection (9:16 AM+-36 min pre; 3:11 PM+-48 min post) rather than an explicit per-runner chip-time finish anchor (p.2).
sample_sets.timepoint_as_reported: prior to the marathon (9:16 AM +- 36 min); marathon started 10:30 AM
sample_sets.assay_platform: Versi-SAL swab collection; SIgA by ELISA (Salimetrics)
sample_sets.n_technical_replicates: duplicate (mean intra-assay CV 2.9% for Study 1, p.5)
sample_sets.pairing_structure: same runners sampled pre and post
sample_sets.age_sex_stratum: NA (All; Men n=150/Women n=60 reported separately in Figure 1 but not analysed as a distinct sample_set here)
sample_sets.preanalytics: Versi-SAL swab under tongue 2 min; stored at 4C in field, transported to lab, centrifuged 1500g 4C 10 min, aliquoted, stored at -80C (p.5).
sample_sets.normalization: Saliva flow rate (FR) = volume/collection time; SIgA secretion rate (SR) = FR x SIgA concentration (density assumed 1.00 g/ml) (p.5).
sample_sets.circadian: Sample collection clock-times reported (9:16 AM pre; 3:11 PM post) but not treated as a controlled circadian factor.
sample_sets.missing_data: 196 of 406 excluded from SIgA analysis: 101 no saliva sample, 84 incomplete dataset, 6 CV>15%, 5 statistical outlier (Figure 1).
sample_sets.sample_notes: Field-based swab method chosen over passive drool for practicality (p.5); pilot data cited showing SIgA stable at 4C for >=3h (journey duration ~20 min).

measurements.measurement_notes: Reported in main text as part of 'Compared with pre-marathon, saliva FR and SIgA SR decreased and SIgA concentration increased post-marathon' and detailed in Supplementary Table S1.
measurements.tested_universe: Targeted saliva panel: flow rate, SIgA concentration, SIgA secretion rate (both studies, p.5).

precision_validation.evidence_notes: [Study1 saliva sIgA/FR/SR vs RTI] ELISA (Salimetrics), mean intra-assay CV for duplicates 2.9% (Study 1); samples with CV>15% excluded (n=6, Figure 1); outliers >3x IQR removed (n=5) (p.5).

[Study1 saliva sIgA/FR/SR vs RTI] Only two timepoints: pre-marathon baseline and an 'immediately after' post sample (time_bin 0_to_lt30min, within_window) with no numeric minutes-post-finish reported; no 30min-72h follow-up saliva sampling. RTI outcome is tracked over a separate 2-week symptom-diary timeline, distinct from the exercise time-bin axis.
[Study1 saliva sIgA/FR/SR vs RTI] SIgA is a well-characterised, specific mucosal antibody; FR/SR are supportive secretion-rate measures rather than independent immune specificities.

[Study1 saliva sIgA/FR/SR vs RTI] Only one pre/post pair per participant, group mean+-SD reported; no repeated baselines, ICC/CV of the biological measure across days, or individual responder/threshold analysis.

precision_validation.temporal_order: Baseline psychological/sIgA measures precede the 2-week RTI follow-up by design; participants reporting RTI symptoms on marathon day itself were excluded to mitigate reverse causation (p.3).
precision_validation.evidence_notes: [Study1 saliva sIgA/FR/SR vs RTI] Explicit null association between mucosal-immunity change (FR, SIgA concentration, SIgA SR) and RTI during the 2 weeks after the marathon (OR~1.00 for all three, p>0.05); RTI itself was self-reported (Jackson common cold questionnaire, >=6 score for >=2 consecutive days) with no pathogen confirmation.
[Study1 saliva sIgA/FR/SR vs RTI] Single field cohort; no replication or external validation of the sIgA-RTI relationship (which was in any case null).

[Study1 saliva sIgA/FR/SR vs RTI] Field-adapted Versi-SAL swab collection chosen specifically for feasibility in a race setting where passive drool was impractical ('not readily available to perform a passive drool', p.5); stability pilot data cited for 4C storage over the ~20 min transport window.
[Study2 saliva sIgA/FR/SR, EX vs CON] Same ELISA platform; mean intra-assay CV 3.3% (Study 2); outliers removed (n=3) (p.5).

[Study2 saliva sIgA/FR/SR, EX vs CON] Three within-window timepoints per trial (pre, immediate post [0_to_lt30min], +30 min post [30min_to_lt3h]) plus a matched non-exercise control trial (matched_control_time); better within-window density than Study 1.
[Study2 saliva sIgA/FR/SR, EX vs CON] Same analytes as Study 1 (SIgA, FR, SR); same specificity considerations.

[Study2 saliva sIgA/FR/SR, EX vs CON] Group mean+-SD by trial/time reported; between-person variability is explored only indirectly via correlation with psychological traits in men (Figure 3: trait anxiety r=-0.59, TMD r=-0.58, state anxiety r=-0.61, perceived stress r=-0.68, all vs change in SIgA SR, p<0.01, n~26) - this characterises some individual variation but is not a formal reliability/responder analysis of the sIgA marker itself.
[Study2 saliva sIgA/FR/SR, EX vs CON] Study 2 is a mechanistic laboratory study with no clinical/infection outcome collected; functional/clinical linkage is not applicable to this sub-study.
[Study2 saliva sIgA/FR/SR, EX vs CON] Single laboratory cohort; no external replication of the EX-vs-CON sIgA response pattern.

[Study2 saliva sIgA/FR/SR, EX vs CON] Controlled laboratory environment (temperature/humidity/pressure/fan speed standardised); passive-drool collection used (more volume-reliable than the field swab, but requires controlled setting) (p.4-5).

ai_assistance.task_prompt_version: 10-report charting pilot, reviewer B AI stand-in instructions (2026-10-05)

extraction_provenance.open_data: Supporting Information S1 (ejsc70058-sup-0001-suppl-data.docx: Supplementary Tables S1-S2, Figures S1-S4) is openly accessible (open-access article); no genomic/omics accession applicable; raw participant-level data not deposited in a public repository as far as reported.
extraction_provenance.integrity_status: No correction/retraction notice visible on the PDF/pages reviewed 2026-10-05; not independently cross-checked against PubMed/Crossref update records beyond the PDF itself.
extraction_provenance.provenance_notes: AI-assisted charting pilot extraction per PILOT_README.md Section 5-7. A docx table-extraction ambiguity (merged cells in Supplementary Table S2's Men/Women columns) limited confident extraction of sex-stratified Study 2 values; only the 'All' column values were used for measurement rows. See unresolved_questions.

eligibility_opinion.rationale: Both sub-studies centre on an identifiable single bout with baseline and post-cessation sampling in adults: Study 1 is the 2017 Snowdonia Marathon with pre-/immediate-post saliva sampling and a 2-week self-reported RTI follow-up (p.2-3); Study 2 is a 60-min treadmill bout at 65% VO2peak with pre/immediate-post/+30min saliva sampling and a seated-rest comparator (p.3-4). Salivary sIgA is a recognized immune mediator (immune_link satisfied); no repeated identified exercise bouts in the same people across >=2 events are reported, so Support B does not apply to either sub-study.

unresolved_questions: Study unit structure: Study 1 (field marathon) and Study 2 (lab crossover) were modelled as two separate study_families/cohorts under one report, since they have different participants, settings and designs; the manual's examples do not explicitly cover a single report with two unrelated sub-studies of this kind, so this structural choice should be confirmed with A/D.

sample_sets.time_bin for Study 1 post-marathon sample: the text gives only 'immediately after the marathon' with clock-times (3:11 PM +-48 min) and no numeric minutes-since-finish; 0_to_lt30min was assigned by interpreting 'immediately' as consistent with other exercise-immunology usage, but this is an inference, not a reported number - flag for calibration of how the manual wants 'immediately after' handled when no numeric offset is given.

Supplementary Table S2 (Study 2) merged-cell parsing: the python-docx extraction of the Men/Women columns produced an inconsistent number of data columns (likely a merged-cell artefact in the original Word table), so sex-stratified EX/CON values could not be confidently extracted; only 'All' values were used in measurement rows. Needs either a corrected supplement re-extraction or a manual recheck against the rendered document.

measurements.result_direction for the group x time ANOVA rows (M-R56-007, M-R56-009): 'mixed_or_inconsistent' was used because the trial main effect was significant overall/in men but not in women, which is a different kind of 'mixed' than a single analyte giving contradictory point estimates; consider whether the vocabulary needs a sex-interaction-specific flag.

precision_validation.functional_clinical_linkage for Study 2: coded as NA because no clinical/infection outcome was collected in this sub-study; confirm this is the intended use of NA (domain not applicable to this design) versus NR (not reported).

reports.author_window_interpretation: the paper never uses 'open window' and its own Study 1 finding is a null sIgA-RTI association; classification as immunosuppression_or_susceptibility_without_term rests on the Introduction's framing of the literature rather than the authors' own conclusions, which could also support no_window_interpretation - flagged for a second reviewer's independent read.

cohorts.older_adult_subgroup / adult_stratum_separable for Study 1: mean ages (46 y men, 43 y women) are noticeably older than Study 2 (22 y); the authors discuss possible peri/post-menopausal status in Study 1 women as a post-hoc explanatory note (p.8) but do not formally define an older-adult subgroup - confirm whether this discussion-section reasoning should trigger an older_adult_subgroup flag even without an author-defined cut-off.
